articles.sourceTitle: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
articles.title: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
articles.text:
Google would certainly prefer that everyone used its Gemini models with Google Cloud services, but soon, you’ll have more options. OpenAI and Google have come to an arrangement that will see the former’s frontier models arrive in Google Cloud services. Perhaps more importantly, GPT models will soon appear in Antigravity, Google’s agent-powered coding tool.
For enterprise customers and AI enthusiasts, OpenAI’s latest model will appear in Google’s “Model Garden” in the coming weeks, adding to its 200-plus options. The garden already offers access to Google’s Gemini models, as well as an assortment of open models like Mistral, Llama, and Gemma. Anthropic’s Claude AI has also been available for some time. Google says it’s now the only large cloud provider offering access to all three leading closed LLMs.
While OpenAI notes that Microsoft continues to be its primary cloud partner, the full suite of current GPT 6 and 6.1 models—Astra, Sol, and Luna—will launch on Google Cloud. Astra will naturally cost the most to run, but Google’s system supports dynamically moving workloads between LLMs based on performance, latency, and efficiency.
OpenAI models will be available to run entirely on Google’s infrastructure, with transactions handled via the Google Cloud Marketplace. For businesses with established Google Cloud spending commitments, this will make it easy to begin using GPT models in place of whatever they were using before.

articles.title: openai/openai-cli: Official CLI for the OpenAI API · GitHub
articles.text:
The official CLI for the OpenAI REST API.

brew install openai/tools/openai

To test or install the CLI locally, you need Go version 1.26 or later installed.
go install 'github.com/openai/openai-cli/cmd/openai@latest'
Once you have run go install, the binary is placed in your Go bin directory:

Default location: $HOME/go/bin (or $GOPATH/bin if GOPATH is set)
Check your path: Run go env GOPATH to see the base directory

If commands aren't found after installation, add the Go bin directory to your PATH:
# Add to your shell profile (.zshrc, .bashrc, etc.)
export PATH="$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin"

The first eligible interactive openai run quietly saves image picker Tab
shortcuts for future Bash, zsh, and fish sessions. Open a new terminal to use
them. See shortcut setup and removal for
requirements and opt-out. PowerShell keeps normal Tab completion; press Enter
after openai images generate to open the picker.

Bare openai checks for newer stable releases when stdin, stdout, and stderr are terminals.
It adds a plain-text notice below help, at most once every seven days.
Explicit help, commands, completion, CI, and redirected streams skip the check entirely.
The notice includes an update command when the CLI can verify its installation method.
Verified Homebrew installations use brew upgrade --cask openai/tools/openai.
Go commands require a verified binary, an available Go command, and an explicit matching GOBIN.
Custom GOOS or GOARCH settings select the installation guide instead.
Go upgrades to major version 2 or later also select the installation guide.
Unknown installations receive the installation-guide link instead.
The CLI never installs updates automatically.
Checks use public GitHub release metadata without API credentials, at most once daily.
Checks respect HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY, including their lowercase forms.
Update discovery waits at most 200 milliseconds. Failed checks remain silent.
Package-manager availability can lag a new GitHub release.
Set OPENAI_CLI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to disable checks and notices.

After cloning the git repository for this project, you can use the
scripts/run script to run the tool locally:

The CLI follows a resource-based command structure:
openai <resource> [subresource...] <command> [flags...]
Standard API endpoints require an API key:
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."

openai responses create \
--input "Say this is a test" \
--model gpt-5.5
Admin endpoints require an admin API key:
export OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY="sk-admin-..."

openai admin organization usage completions \
--start-time 1735689600 \
--end-time 1735776000 \
--bucket-width 1d
Browse each group with --help, for example openai admin --help or
openai admin organization --help. Existing colon commands such as
openai admin:organization:usage completions continue to work.
Run openai to browse command groups by task, with descriptions for each group.
Group help separates actions from nested command groups and lists every immediate command.
Help works without an API key or network connection:
openai help setup                  # Enter your API key safely
openai images generate --help      # Example and every image option
openai help images generate        # The same complete image help
openai --help                      # Command groups and global options
Add --help (or -h) to any command for its complete help page.
openai help COMMAND shows the same page.
Command pages list global options. Use openai --help for their full descriptions.
You can place --help after valid command options.
The old help --all spelling prints migration guidance and the complete page.
Command behavior, defaults, and output formats remain unchanged.
Tab completion follows the same group order and supports help topics and file input paths.
After upgrading, reload shell completion to enable the new file-path behavior.
Older loaded completion scripts keep their previous behavior until refreshed.
Enable command insertion to fill your command line
from examples, setup guidance, and recovery commands. Ctrl+X, then Tab searches suggestions
without running them. Double Tab is an optional binding for Bash, zsh, and fish.
Successful JSON responses print readable text by default, including in pipes.
Use --format json or --format jsonl in scripts that parse API data.
See reading command results for extraction, binary
output, and the scope of readable presentation.
Upload a local file with an explicit purpose, inspect its metadata, then download its contents:
openai files upload "upload space.txt" --purpose user_data
openai files get file-example
openai files download file-example --output "downloaded copy.txt"
openai files download file-example > copy.txt
Replace file-example with the returned file ID. Upload takes a plain path, without an added @.
create, retrieve, content, and their existing flags remain available.
See working with files for literal filenames, output formats, and script examples.
openai images generate --prompt "A tiny orange robot" saves images to
~/Downloads/gpt-images/ and prints their paths, including in pipes. The CLI
uses gpt-image-2.5-sunburst when saving without an explicit model or legacy
response format. Use --model for another exact ID, --name for a filename,
or --output-dir for an existing directory. Existing files are kept.
--format json returns API data without saving or applying the CLI preset.
images edit also saves new results while keeping source files.
images create-variation is retired and no longer available. To create a
variation, use images edit with a GPT Image model and a prompt. See
image generation and saving for commands
and defaults.
openai images preview "path/to/image.png" redisplays a saved image without an
API request. Use openai images inline on or off to remember whether future
saved images appear automatically. Per-command --inline auto, on or off
overrides that setting. on also permits an image font in local Apple Terminal.
Errors print actionable summaries to stderr by default. Use --format-error json
for original API error details, including unknown fields and SDK-reported stream
error events. For those events, extraction paths include the error envelope,
for example --transform-error error.code. Explicit --format
values json, jsonl, raw, and yaml also apply to errors unless overridden
by --format-error; an explicit --format-error auto or text restores summaries.
--transform-error extracts error data independently of successful output.
Malformed or empty error bodies receive a safe diagnostic; HTTP status is included
only when the SDK retains it. Summaries omit rejected values and request URLs;
explicit API error details can contain server-supplied sensitive data.

Environment variable
Required
Default value

OPENAI_API_KEY
no
null

OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY
no
null

OPENAI_ORG_ID
no
null

OPENAI_PROJECT_ID
no
null

OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET
no
null

OPENAI_CUSTOM_HEADERS
no
null

OPENAI_MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_FILE
no
null

OPENAI_MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_FILE
no

OPENAI_UNTRUSTED_STDIN
no
false

--api-key (can also be set with OPENAI_API_KEY env var)
--admin-api-key (can also be set with OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY env var)
--organization (can also be set with OPENAI_ORG_ID env var)
--project (can also be set with OPENAI_PROJECT_ID env var)
--webhook-secret (can also be set with OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var)
--mtls-client-cert-file (can also be set with OPENAI_MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_FILE env var)
--mtls-client-key-file (can also be set with OPENAI_MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_FILE env var)
--help - Show command line usage
--debug - Enable debug logging. This includes HTTP request/response details and bodies; do not share debug logs if they may contain sensitive payloads.
--version, -v - Show the CLI version
--base-url - Use a custom API backend URL. HTTPS is required except for
localhost or literal loopback IP addresses such as 127.0.0.1 and ::1.
This also applies to OPENAI_BASE_URL; remote HTTP backends must enable HTTPS.
--header, -H - Add a literal request header as Name: Value; repeat for multiple headers
--format - Change the output format (auto, text, explore, json, jsonl, pretty, raw, yaml); auto selects readable text unless extracting data
--format-error - Change the stderr error format (auto, text, explore, json, jsonl, pretty, raw, yaml); auto selects readable summaries unless extracting error data
--transform - Transform the data output using GJSON syntax
--transform-error - Transform the error output using GJSON syntax

Use --header or -H before or after a resource command:
openai --header 'X-Trace-ID: example-123' models list \
-H 'X-Client-Label: local,manual'
Values are literal: commas and colons are preserved, and @ prefixes do not
read files. Surrounding spaces and tabs are trimmed from values. -H 'X-Example:'
sends an empty value. If a name is repeated, the last value wins regardless of
case, overriding default and endpoint-specific headers. Headers managed by the
HTTP transport, such as Host and Content-Length, retain the transport's
behavior. Supplied header values are hidden in help and redacted in debug logs.
For credential-bearing headers, have a secret manager or trusted launcher set
OPENAI_CUSTOM_HEADERS directly in the CLI's environment. This keeps credentials
out of command arguments and avoids typing literal secrets into shell history.
The variable accepts one Name: Value entry per line. For example, with
non-sensitive values:
export OPENAI_CUSTOM_HEADERS='X-Trace-ID: example-123
X-Client-Label: local,manual'
openai models list
--header and endpoint-specific header flags override matching environment
entries. Environment header values are also redacted in debug logs. Use
OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY for standard API and admin authentication.

Mutual TLS is currently in beta. To opt in and activate a CA certificate for
your organization or project, follow the
OpenAI Mutual TLS Beta Program
instructions.
To authenticate API-key requests with a mutual TLS client certificate, provide
the client certificate and private key as separate PEM files. If certificate
chain support is enabled for your organization, the certificate file must
contain the leaf certificate first, followed by any intermediate certificates.
Otherwise, use a client certificate signed directly by an activated CA
certificate.
export OPENAI_MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_FILE=/run/secrets/openai/client-chain.pem
export OPENAI_MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/openai/client.key
export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://mtls.api.openai.com/v1

openai files list
Both mTLS files must be configured together. Keep the private key in a
permission-restricted file; do not put private-key contents directly in command
arguments or environment variables. The CLI does not automatically select an
mTLS endpoint, so configure OPENAI_BASE_URL or --base-url explicitly. HTTP
and SOCKS proxies remain supported, but HTTPS proxies are rejected to prevent
presenting the client certificate during the proxy's own TLS handshake.
Passing files as arguments
For JSON input values, @myfile.ext reads local file contents:
Binary upload flags use plain paths. For example, use files upload --file "upload space.txt" --purpose user_data.
Here, --file "@upload space.txt" names an actual file starting with @; it does not expand another file reference.
See working with files.
openai <command> --arg @abe.jpg
Files can also be passed inside JSON or YAML blobs:
openai <command> --arg '{image: "@abe.jpg"}'
# Equivalent:
openai <command> <<YAML
arg:
image: "@abe.jpg"
YAML
When piping JSON or YAML from an untrusted source, enable untrusted-stdin mode:
untrusted-producer | OPENAI_UNTRUSTED_STDIN=1 openai <command> --file ./upload.txt
In this mode, values supplied through stdin are treated as literal data: @,
@file://, and @data:// references in request bodies, headers, and query
parameters do not read local files. File-upload parameters must be provided
explicitly as command-line flags. Explicit flags retain their normal file
behavior and take precedence over values supplied through std

PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE in PHP
articles.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet
articles.text: Executive SummaryWiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them. PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others.These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it, putting every affected website in immediate risk. Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised.On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine. These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability  required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.OverviewIn this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure.Nearly every PHP version is affected by at least one of these issues, including releases dating back to PHP 5.4. The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory. That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself.PHP is the programming language behind much of the web, powering WordPress, Drupal and MediaWiki, the software that runs Wikipedia. A flaw in its core engine can affect websites across this ecosystem, even when their own application code is secure.Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security. In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet. In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify. We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities. Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.Wiz Research would like to thank the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI for their work on discovery, coordination and patch verification. OpenAI and Calif also published blogs containing details on the vulnerability – its history, technical details, and insight into the disclosure process. PHP posted as well.We’d also like to express our sincere gratitude towards Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare, Fastly, Google, Imperva, Microsoft, Vercel, and many others, for helping prepare guidance and out-of-the-box mitigations for customers who cannot apply the patch immediately.The VulnerabilitiesAll of the disclosed vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues that stem from bugs in how PHP handles fatal errors while processing requests, particularly out-of-memory errors. These bugs can leave a corrupted internal PHP state behind after a request ends unexpectedly. A later request or worker can reuse that stale state, leading to memory disclosure or corruption.Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP. The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations. They are representative targets - exploitation does not require one of these CMSs, as the vulnerable code is in PHP itself.While this blog covers only four instances of exploitable bugs (grouped under two CVEs) that follow this problematic pattern, there are other tracked, and likely untracked, variants of this issue in the PHP codebase. These variants have different requirements for exploitation and can lead to different types of impact. In any case, the patch provided by the PHP team fixes the issue at its core and eliminates all variants in the patched release.ImpactWe combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress (wordpress:latest), Drupal (drupal:latest), and Joomla (joomla:latest), using their latest container images at the time of testing.These platforms illustrate the impact, but the vulnerabilities are in PHP itself. Exploitation does not depend on a flaw in the application’s code: even a simple “Hello World” application running on an affected PHP version can be vulnerable.Separately, we demonstrated that attackers could read sensitive data from the PHP process’s memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys, without needing to achieve remote code execution.Demonstrations of PHP2Shell with Wordpress, Joomla, and Drupal: The AI inflection pointThe vulnerable code had been present for more than a decade. Turning these flaws into working exploits required chaining multiple bugs and accounting for how PHP allocates and reuses memory across requests. Memory bugs are notoriously complex; differences in PHP versions, configurations and application behavior can break assumptions the exploit depends on. An attack that works against one deployment may need substantial adjustments to work against another, each requiring further analysis, testing and debugging. Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale. With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts. With testing and debugging tools, models can analyze failures and iterate on adjustments, reducing the specialist effort required for each target. This significantly lowers the barrier to scaling attacks across different deployments.This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. As AI reduces the effort needed to develop and adapt complex exploits, vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets. We used Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research. Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.Using Gemini 4 Argon, the team at Wiz has shown why frontier AI is a game-changer for cyber defense. For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex. We're pleased to see Gemini 4 Argon help defenders bridge that gap, finding vulnerabilities and helping patch them.Raluca Ada Popa, Head of Gemini Security, Google DeepMindIndustry-level collaborationsPrior to public disclosure, Wiz Research worked with the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI on discovery, coordination and patch verification. We also partnered with Google Cloud, Cloudflare, AWS, Microsoft, Automattic, Fastly, Akamai, Imperva, Vercel and many others to prepare customer guidance, detections and out-of-the-box mitigations for organizations that cannot update immediately.A vulnerability in core PHP reaches far beyond a single application. PHP runs across clouds, hosting providers, content-delivery networks and millions of independently managed servers. Reducing exposure before the technical details became public required coordinated work across that entire ecosystem.Technical deep diveBug: Upload-progress unserializer use-after-freePHP's Session module can decode session data during upload-progress handling in the same pre-initialization window. The decoder stores request-owned bookkeeping in BG(unserialize). A fatal allocation failure can interrupt this path, destroy the request heap and leave the unserializer's global state published.On a later request handled by the same worker, PHP can consume attacker-reclaimed memory as live unserializer bookkeeping. The stale state becomes a powerful memory-corruption primitive. We combined it with the memory disclosure to remove address uncertainty and achieved unauthenticated remote code execution on WordPress, Drupal and Joomla.The WordPress, Drupal and Joomla chains are representative demonstrations. The underlying primitives exist at the PHP engine level and can affect any PHP application running on a vulnerable version.These issues execute below the application layer, so application logs may contain little context. Until systems are patched, defenders should pay particular attention to unusual multipart requests followed by memory-limit errors or repeated HTTP 500 responses, unexpectedly large or malformed PHPSESSID response cookies, and unexplained PHP worker churn. These signals can guide an investigation. Applying the PHP security update remains the only complete remediation.Bug: Remote process-memory disclosurePHP parses RFC1867 multipart requests during request startup, before normal module initialization has completed. Session upload-progress handling can initialize Session state at this early stage and publish a session ID in PS(id). An out-of-memory error can abort the request before cleanup completes. PHP then destroys the request heap and may leave PS(id) pointing to the freed allocation.A later multipart request handled by the same worker can reach the upload-progress cleanup path before normal Session initialization resets that pointer. PHP trusts the stale pointer and length as a live zend_string and URL-encodes the reclaimed heap contents into a PHPSESSID response cookie. The attack works even when the application never calls session_start(), making the issue application-agnostic. We demonstrated unauthenticated disclosure of an attacker-sized region of live worker memory containing data from outside the attacker's request.Bug: Fatal-error backtrace use-after-freeIn affected versions, PHP retains the backtrace of the most recent fatal error in EG(last_fatal_error_backtrace). A fatal out-of-memory error can destroy the request heap without undefining that executor-global value. The worker survives with a global that still points to memory from the previous request.If the same worker emits a diagnostic early in the next request, it can access the pointer before the executor reinitializes that state. PHP then destroys or updates the dangling backtrace and follows attacker-reclaimed memory. The resulting cross-request use-after-free can be developed into controlled memory corruption.
